overall: Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law: the Purpose 3 executive session on the silt fence right-of-way was proper, roll call and purpose announcement were done, and the open-session description was sufficient. Open minutes should note the executive session, but no order issued.

allegations.summary: Complainants alleged the Board convened in executive session for an improper purpose after they had withdrawn their reimbursement request and asked that the topic be removed from the agenda.
allegations.key_passage: We conclude that the Board's consideration of whether to initiate legal action against the complainants was demonstrably likely to proceed if the complainants did not comply with its demand to remove the silt fence from the Town's right-of-way by April 1.

allegations.summary: Complainants alleged the Board failed to follow executive session procedures, namely the roll call vote and the announcement of the reason for the executive session.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the Board did comply with the requisite procedures, as reflected in the executive session minutes, though the open session minutes do not include any mention of an executive session or the procedural steps.

allegations.summary: Tied to the procedural claim, the AG assessed whether the chair's open-session description of the executive session purpose, which omitted the litigation's specifics, was sufficient.
allegations.key_passage: Accordingly, we find that Board's open session description of the executive session was sufficient and did not violate the Open Meeting Law.
